# FG-CI-0015

| 項目 | 値 |
|---|---|
| HTTP ステータス | 503 |
| 重大度 | alert |
| Runbook | [`ci-runner`](../../ops/runbooks/ci-runner.md) |
| 発生させるテスト | `configured_default_volumes_stop_the_runner_before_any_job` |

## 利用者向けメッセージ

- ja: CI の Runner が、ジョブのコンテナを Runner から切り離せていることを確かめられませんでした。Runner はジョブを実行しません。管理者に連絡してください。
- en: The CI runner could not verify that a job's container is kept apart from the runner. The runner runs no jobs. Contact the administrator.
- id: Runner CI tidak dapat memastikan bahwa kontainer tugas terpisah dari runner. Runner tidak menjalankan tugas. Hubungi administrator.

## 原因 (cause)

ADR-0029 amendment 2026-11-12: a job's container must get nothing from a containers.conf beyond what the runner's flags ask for. Found on the test runner: the quay.io/podman/stable image ships `volumes = ["/proc:/proc"]` and host IPC/UTS/cgroup namespaces, and every job saw the runner's /proc (every process of the runner, of other jobs and of their services) and shared its IPC/UTS. So Podman reads only the runner's own containers.conf, `<work_dir>/runner/podman/containers.conf` (rewritten at every start, passed as `CONTAINERS_CONF` on every Podman call, with an empty `mounts.conf` and OCI hooks directory beside it; no system or user containers.conf and no drop-in is read), every Podman call has a cleared environment, and before every claim (and at start and in `forge-runner check`) the runner creates a probe container `forge-isolation-probe-<pid>` like a service (no `--volume`), never started, from the empty directory `<work_dir>/runner/empty-rootfs` (`--rootfs`, no pull), reads `podman inspect` and removes it. `reason=unexpected_config` with `key` (the first of `Mounts`, `Binds`, `Devices`, `CapAdd`, `Sysctls`, `Privileged`, `SecurityOpt`, `PidMode`, `IpcMode`, `UTSMode`, `CgroupMode`, `UsernsMode`, `ShmSize`, `Annotations`, `Env`) and `deviations` (all of them; for `Env` only the variable names, never values): something other than the runner changed what Podman makes — its containers.conf was edited after the start, or `CONTAINERS_CONF` is not honoured by this Podman. `reason=probe_failed` with `step` (`create` / `inspect` / `remove` / `stale`), `exit_code` or `timeout_ms`, `podman_stderr`, `remove_failed` (the probe's removal also failed) or `parse` (the inspect output was not a container's JSON): Podman itself failed, so isolation is unverified. `reason=conf_unwritable`: the runner could not write its containers.conf. In every case the runner takes no job: at start it exits non-zero, while running it stops before the next claim (a systemd `Restart=on-failure` starts it again, and it stops again until fixed).

## 調べ方 (diagnosis)

The runner host (`journalctl -u forge-runner`, JSON) logs it once (alert) with `error_code`, `request_id` and `context` `reason`, `key`, `deviations` or `step` / `exit_code` / `podman_stderr`; pending jobs wait (FG-CI-0005 after 10 minutes, `forge doctor` `ci.runners`). `forge-runner check` prints the same code. As the runner's user (read-only): `cat <work_dir>/runner/podman/containers.conf` (compare with a fresh start: it is rewritten), `ls <work_dir>/runner/podman/hooks.d`, `podman --version` (4.x or later honours CONTAINERS_CONF), `podman ps -a --filter name=forge-isolation-probe-`.

## 対処 (fix)

Follow runbook ci-runner (Job isolation): for `unexpected_config` find what edits the runner's directory or makes Podman ignore CONTAINERS_CONF (a wrapper script for `podman`, an old Podman), fix it and restart the runner (the containers.conf is rewritten); for `probe_failed` repair Podman as for FG-CI-0007 (rootless setup, storage) and restart; for `conf_unwritable` make `<work_dir>/runner` writable by the runner's user. Changes on the host need human approval.
